summary: A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Camille Bulcke earned degrees from KU Leuven, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad. He served as Head of the Sanskrit and Hindi Department at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, from 1949 to 1957.

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Camillo Alessio Formigatti studied at the University of Milan and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Jürgen Hanneder. His career includes posts at Cambridge, Würzburg, Oxford, and the Bodleian Library.

An Indologist, Canan Yoğurt completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Ankara University and postgraduate work at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. She held research posts at Erciyes University (2014-2024), the University of Hyderabad (2017), and Çukurova University (2024).

A scholar in linguistics, Carel Gabriel Cobet attended Gymnasium Haganum and studied at Leiden University (~1832-1836). He later held academic appointments at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.
Active in religious studies, Carl A. P. Ruck studied at the University of Michigan (~1957-1960) and Harvard University (~1960-1965). He held a post at Boston University around 1970.

A specialist in Sinology and linguistics, Carl Arendt studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Heymann Steinthal (1856-1859). He subsequently served as a Lehrer at the Seminar for Oriental Languages from 1887 to 1902.

Working in linguistics and history/archaeology, Carl Bezold studied under Friedrich Delitzsch (~1879-1883). He founded the Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und Vorderasiatische Archäologie in 1886 and held a post at Heidelberg University from approximately 1894 to 1922.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Carl Bielefeldt studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Seizan Yanagida, and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley. He served on the editorial board and as emeritus professor at Stanford University (~1980-2013).

Carl Brockelmann worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at Rostock, Breslau, and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke, he held professorships at Breslau (1893-1903, 1923-1935), Königsberg (1903-1910), Halle-Wittenberg (1910-1922), and Berlin (1910-1923).

Carl Cappeller, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Humboldt University under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena. He held a professorship at the University of Jena from 1875 to 1921.
Carl Christian Rafn was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Copenhagen from approximately 1814 to 1816 and later held a post there.

An Indologist and linguist, Carl Darling Buck studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He served as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative IE Philology at the University of Chicago (1892-1933).

A historian and archaeologist, Carl Ferdinand Friedrich Lehmann-Haupt held academic positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893-1910), Istanbul University (~1915-1918), the University of Innsbruck (~1918-1932), and the University of Greifswald.

An Indologist and linguist, Carl Fredrik Bergstedt earned a degree at Uppsala University (1836-1842) under Otto Fredrik Tullberg. He also studied under Christian Lassen (~1844-1845), Eugène Burnouf (~1845-1846), and Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1846-1848).

Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at TU Braunschweig, Göttingen under Georg Christoph Lichtenberg and Christian Gottlob Heyne, and Helmstedt. He served as a full professor at the University of Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory from 1807 to 1855.

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Carl Friedrich Lottner studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1851-1854). He later held posts at Trinity College, Hartford, as a Lecturer (1860) and Professor of Sanskrit (1864).

Working in Indology and linguistics, Carl Gaedicke completed his PhD at the University of Jena in 1877 under doctoral supervisor Berthold Delbrück. He also studied under Eduard Sievers and Carl Cappeller.

Working in religious studies and medicine, Carl Gustav Jung studied at the University of Basel (1895-1900). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905-1914), ETH Zurich (1933-1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

A scholar in religious studies and Indology, Carl Gustav Ruben Diehl earned degrees at Lund University between 1925 and 1956. He served as a Docent at Lund University (1954-1959) and Uppsala University (1960-1966).

Carl Hjalmar Borgstrøm, a linguist and Indologist, completed his MA at the University of Oslo (1928-1936). He held posts at Trinity College Dublin (1932-1935), Ankara University (1936-1937), Lund University (1945), and the University of Oslo (1947-1976).
